target: Vocês precisariam de quantas cadeiras?
english: How many chairs would you need?
tip: Precisar needs de before its object: precisariam de quantas cadeiras, how many chairs you would need.

target: Torço para que o Brasil ganhe.
english: I'm rooting for Brazil to win.
tip: Torcer literally means to wring, but torcer para is the verb for rooting for a team: torço para o Brasil.

target: Até que prove o contrário, confio nele.
english: Unless proven otherwise, I trust him.
tip: Confiar pairs with em, and em plus ele contracts to nele: confio nele means I trust him.

target: Embora ela seja jovem, é muito madura.
english: Although she's young, she's very mature.
tip: Embora means although and always takes the subjunctive: embora ela seja jovem, not é jovem.

target: Não acho que valha a pena reclamar.
english: I don't think it's worth complaining.
tip: Valer a pena means to be worth the trouble: valha a pena reclamar means worth complaining.

target: Vai com calma, não precisa ter pressa.
english: Take it easy, there's no rush.
tip: Portuguese has haste rather than being in a hurry: ter pressa, so não precisa ter pressa means no need to rush.

target: Presta atenção no que eu estou dizendo.
english: Pay attention to what I'm saying.
tip: Prestar atenção means to pay attention and takes em: presta atenção no is em plus o que.

target: Duvido que ele se lembre do meu aniversário.
english: I doubt he'll remember my birthday.
tip: Lembrar meaning to remember uses the reflexive with de: ele se lembre do aniversário.

target: Experimenta esse bolo, ficou ótimo.
english: Try this cake, it turned out great.
tip: Experimentar means to try or taste food, not to experiment: experimenta esse bolo means try this cake.

target: Respire fundo e se acalme.
english: Take a deep breath and calm down.
tip: Respirar fundo means to breathe deeply, with fundo working as an adverb here, not fundamente.

target: Não conheço ninguém que fale japonês.
english: I don't know anyone who speaks Japanese.
tip: When the person might not exist, the relative verb goes subjunctive: ninguém que fale, not fala.

target: Mesmo que você tente, não vai conseguir.
english: Even if you try, you won't succeed.
tip: Mesmo que means even if and takes the subjunctive: mesmo que você tente, not tenta.

target: Antes que eu esqueça, anota meu telefone.
english: Before I forget, write down my number.
tip: Antes que means before and triggers the subjunctive: antes que eu esqueça, not esqueço.

target: Os amigos com quem saí ontem são do trabalho.
english: The friends I went out with yesterday are from work.
tip: English can strand the preposition ('friends I went out with'); Portuguese fronts it: com quem saí.

target: Espera um minutinho.
english: Wait a moment.
tip: The ending -inho shrinks and softens a word: minutinho is a little minute, meaning just a quick moment.

target: Não toque nisso!
english: Don't touch that!
tip: A positive command to a friend is toca, but negating it flips to the subjunctive: não toque.

target: Larga de ser teimoso.
english: Stop being stubborn.
tip: Largar de plus a verb is a casual way to say stop doing something: larga de ser teimoso.

target: Você deveria descansar mais.
english: You should rest more.
tip: 'Deveria' (should) is the conditional of 'dever' – softer than 'deve'.

target: Faz um favor pra mim.
english: Do me a favor.
tip: After a preposition use mim, not eu: pra mim means for me.

target: Me conta o que aconteceu.
english: Tell me what happened.
tip: Brazilian Portuguese puts the object pronoun before the verb, even at the start: Me conta.

target: Faz as pazes com ela.
english: Make up with her.
tip: Fazer as pazes is a set phrase meaning to make up or make peace.

target: Vocês vão precisar de passaporte.
english: You'll need a passport.
tip: Precisar always takes de before what you need: precisar de passaporte.

target: Você aceitaria um café?
english: Would you like a coffee?
tip: The conditional ending -ria turns a question into a polite offer: aceitaria um café.

target: Leia as instruções antes de começar.
english: Read the instructions before starting.
tip: Antes de is followed by the plain infinitive, not a conjugated verb: antes de começar.

target: Escova os dentes antes de dormir.
english: Brush your teeth before bed.
tip: With body parts Portuguese uses the article, not a possessive: os dentes means your teeth.

target: Não demore, a gente está esperando.
english: Don't take long, we're waiting.
tip: A gente means we but takes a singular verb: a gente está.

target: Nós vamos conversar sobre isso depois.
english: We'll talk about this later.
tip: 'Vamos + infinitive' expresses future plans for 'we' – also used for suggestions ('Vamos comer?').

target: Põe a roupa pra lavar.
english: Put the clothes in the wash.
tip: The verb pôr is irregular; its command form is põe: põe a roupa.

target: Leva o cachorro pra passear.
english: Take the dog for a walk.
tip: Levar is take away from the speaker; trazer is bring toward: leva o cachorro.

target: Guarda a louça no armário.
english: Put the dishes in the cabinet.
tip: Guardar means to put away or store, not to guard: guarda a louça.
